searches.note: Twenty one searches of a share of twenty eight, none the author's. Eleven were restricted to a producer's or a wine body's domain (lyrarakis.com four times, douloufakis.wine three times, alexakiswines.com twice with winesofcrete.gr, manousakiswinery.com, winesofgreece.org) and read as primary for the house's own facts. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
What a search contradicted was set right with its source; what rested on no source was cut; sources whose address names a living critic were met and are not cited.

tested: Founding 1966 by two brothers at Alagni: lyrarakis.com about page, Berry Bros and Wines of Crete; kept.
Plyto and Dafni planted at Psarades in 1992, first single grape bottlings 1996: about page and the house's sustainability report; story set to 1996.
Altitude: about page and the labels of 2022 to 2025 all give 480 metres; set to about 480.
Melissaki: the house's Melissaki page, found at the foot of Psiloritis and planted in the Gerodeti vineyard in 2010; reworded.
Aggelis: the house's page, ungrafted old Liatiko in eastern Crete; note reworded.

Glass and serving: the house's sheets of 2023, 2024 and 2025 (white peach, pear, quince, chalky and shellfish notes, rich and full, a herbal finish; 10 to 12 degrees Celsius; 40 per cent of the 2024 a month and a half in oak); glass rewritten, serve and making kept.
The obstacles from state agencies: the house's sustainability report; kept as its own telling.

livingNamesMet: Lyrarakis: the founding brothers Manolis and Sotiris Lyrarakis (living or dead not settled; not named).
Douloufakis: the founder Dimitris, his son George and the grandson Nikos Douloufakis (no dates found; not named).
Alexakis: the founders Stelios and Sofia Alexakis and their sons Lazaros and Apostolos.
Manousakis: the founder Theodore (Ted) Manousakis, his daughter Alexandra, and the advisers Lucie Morton, Pascal Marchand, Laurence Feraud, Bruce Zoecklein and Yves Herody.
Others met in sources: Franz Keller (the Baden estate where Economou worked), the critics Yiannis Karakasis, Jancis Robinson and Jamie Goode; none is named in the fragment.
swaps: No swap proposed. The author noted Alexakis as thin and named Idaia, Silva Daskalaki or Diamantakis as alternatives without proposing; the refuter rules Alexakis stays: the house, the producers' association and two trade sources confirm its Vidiano, its making is on its own page, and the thin region rule allows a large house said plainly to be one.
codexTension: The region summary calls Vidiano the rising star of apricot and herbs; it agrees with the records. No library record exists for any of the five houses. No Codex record was edited.
